This figure only shows the organizational form of tourism routes and does not contain the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway route, terrain water systems, or river names, so the rivers along the way cannot be read directly from the figure. Reasoning: The question stem states that the tourist's final section is "taking high-speed rail from Shanghai back to Beijing," and explicitly asks "if taking the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway back to Beijing." Therefore the question is transformed into: from Shanghai northward to Beijing, which major rivers in eastern China does the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway pass along the way? In spatial order from south to north, after departing from Shanghai it is located in the lower Yangtze River region and will pass the Yangtze River; continuing northward enters the Huai River basin and will pass the Huai River; farther north reaches the lower Yellow River region and will pass the Yellow River; approaching the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region belongs to the Hai River system and will pass the Hai River. Therefore the answer is Yangtze River, Huai River, Yellow River, Hai River.
